title: Linear optical fan-out gates using fewer ancillary single photons with enhanced success probability
abstract: Photonic quantum gates are fundamental building blocks for a wide range of optical quantum information processing tasks. We propose an efficient linear-optical scheme for implementing a post-selected three-qubit fan-out gate (also known as a controlled-NOT-NOT gate) using only two ancillary single photons and linear optical elements. The scheme can be generalized to an $n$-qubit fan-out gate, requiring $(n-1)$ ancillary single photons and $(3n-3)$ polarizing beam splitters (PBSs), with a success probability of $\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{n-1}$. Compared to the standard gate decomposition approach, which requires $(2n-2)$ ancillary single photons, $(5n-5)$ PBSs, and yields a success probability of $\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{n-1}$. Our scheme significantly reduces the resource overhead and improves the success probability. We further evaluate the gate performance and demonstrate improved robustness compared to gate decomposition-based methods.
summary: This paper presents an optimized linear-optical scheme to realize $n$-qubit fan-out quantum gates ($C_n$) using photons. The proposed method significantly reduces the required ancillary resources (photons and PBSs) compared to conventional gate decomposition techniques. This improvement leads to a higher success probability and better overall performance for photonic quantum information processing.

main_result: The proposed scheme successfully implements the $n$-qubit fan-out gate using significantly fewer ancillary single photons and polarizing beam splitters (PBSs) compared to standard decomposition methods. This results in an improved success probability of $\left( rac{1}{4}ight)^{n-1}$.
method: The authors propose a novel linear optical scheme involving sequential interference steps at PBSs, utilizing ancillary single photons and Hadamard operations via Half-Wave Plates (HWPs). The process relies on post-selection based on coincidence measurements.
model_or_system: The physical platform is photonic quantum information processing using polarization states ($|Hangle, |Vangle$) of single photons. The scheme uses linear optical elements like PBSs and HWPs to mediate the multi-qubit gate operation.

paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of efficient linear-optical fan-out gates, details the novel scheme for $	ext{C}^3$, generalizes it to $C_n$, provides detailed resource comparisons against existing methods (GDM), and concludes with fidelity analysis considering experimental imperfections.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of photonic quantum computation by offering a more resource-efficient architecture for complex multi-qubit gates, which are crucial building blocks for scalable quantum networks and algorithms.
